associations.rationale: The type only constructs a linear map from the dual space to endomorphisms of Spinor; it does not expose that the operators are contraction or state the proof claim.
The type supplies the creation-operator map into End(Spinor), a construction used in the concrete model, but does not itself state the claimed contraction action or irreducibility.
The type constructs an even-dimensional Clifford algebra action on Spinor; it is a representation construction rather than a statement of the requested proof's irreducibility conclusion.

The type directly states simplicity of the transported even-dimensional Spinor module, but this is only the irreducibility component and does not state the full construction, contraction, and odd-parity-actions claim.
The type constructs the hyperbolic Clifford action on Spinor, which is part of the concrete model but does not itself assert irreducibility.
The type directly states simplicity of the hyperbolic Spinor module, but this is only the irreducibility component and does not state the full construction, contraction, and odd-parity-actions claim.
The type constructs one odd-dimensional Clifford action on Spinor, serving as one of the parity-action constructions rather than a theorem stating the full source claim.
The type constructs the other odd-dimensional Clifford action on Spinor, serving as the companion parity-action construction rather than stating the full proof claim.

The type asserts simplicity for an odd Spinor module, but the displayed conclusion does not identify a minus parity module and is an additional result beyond merely constructing the two parity actions.

The type asserts simplicity for an odd Spinor module, but the displayed conclusion does not identify a plus parity module and is an additional result beyond merely constructing the two parity actions.
The type states that SpinorPlus and SpinorMinus admit no module linear equivalence; their nonisomorphism is a consequence beyond the source's construction of the two actions.

The type classifies every simple odd Clifford module as isomorphic to one of the two spinors, a stronger classification consequence rather than the construction-and-irreducibility proof described by the source.
